  "name": "immer",
  "version": "10.0.3-beta",
  "description": "Create your next immutable state by mutating the current one",
  "main": "./dist/cjs/index.js",
  "module": "./dist/immer.legacy-esm.js",
  "exports": {
    "./package.json": "./package.json",
    ".": {
      "react-native": {
        "types": "./dist/immer.d.ts",
        "default": "./dist/immer.legacy-esm.js"
      },
      "import": {
        "types": "./dist/immer.d.ts",
        "default": "./dist/immer.mjs"
      },
      "require": {
        "types": "./dist/immer.d.ts",
        "default": "./dist/cjs/index.js"
      }
    }
  },
  "jsnext:main": "dist/immer.mjs",
  "source": "src/immer.ts",
  "types": "./dist/immer.d.ts",
  "sideEffects": false,
  "scripts": {
    "test": "vitest run && yarn test:build && yarn test:flow",
    "test:perf": "cd __performance_tests__ && node add-data.mjs && node todo.mjs && node incremental.mjs && node large-obj.mjs",
    "test:flow": "yarn flow check __tests__/flow",
    "test:build": "yarn build && vitest run --config vitest.config.build.ts",
    "test:src": "vitest run",
    "watch": "vitest",

    "publish-docs": "cd website && GIT_USER=mweststrate USE_SSH=true yarn docusaurus deploy",
    "start": "cd website && yarn start",
    "test:size": "yarn build && yarn import-size --report . produce enableMapSet enablePatches enableArrayMethods",
    "test:sizequick": "yarn build && yarn import-size . produce",
    "release": "semantic-release --branches main"

  "husky": {
    "hooks": {
      "pre-commit": "pretty-quick --staged"

    "url": "https://github.com/immerjs/immer/issues"

    "dist",
    "compat",
    "src"
  ],
  "devDependencies": {
    "@babel/core": "^7.21.3",
    "@types/node": "^24.3.1",
    "@vitest/coverage-v8": "2.1.9",
    "coveralls": "^3.0.0",
    "cpx2": "^3.0.0",
    "deep-freeze": "^0.0.1",
    "flow-bin": "^0.123.0",
    "husky": "^1.2.0",
    "immutable": "^3.8.2",
    "import-size": "^1.0.2",
    "lodash": "^4.17.4",
    "lodash.clonedeep": "^4.5.0",
    "prettier": "3.8.0",
    "pretty-quick": "^4.2.2",
    "redux": "^4.0.5",
    "rimraf": "^2.6.2",
    "seamless-immutable": "^7.1.3",
    "semantic-release": "^25.0.3",

    "type-plus": "^7.6.2",
    "typescript": "^5.0.2",

import {
	IProduce,
	IProduceWithPatches,
	Immer,
	Draft,
	Immutable
} from "./internal"

export {
	Draft,
	WritableDraft,
	Immutable,
	Patch,
	PatchListener,
	Producer,
	original,
	current,
	isDraft,
	isDraftable,
	NOTHING as nothing,
	DRAFTABLE as immerable,
	freeze,
	Objectish,
	StrictMode
} from "./internal"

const immer = new Immer()

/**
 * The `produce` function takes a value and a "recipe function" (whose
 * return value often depends on the base state). The recipe function is
 * free to mutate its first argument however it wants. All mutations are
 * only ever applied to a __copy__ of the base state.
 *
 * Pass only a function to create a "curried producer" which relieves you
 * from passing the recipe function every time.
 *
 * Only plain objects and arrays are made mutable. All other objects are
 * considered uncopyable.
 *
 * Note: This function is __bound__ to its `Immer` instance.
 *
 * @param {any} base - the initial state
 * @param {Function} producer - function that receives a proxy of the base state as first argument and which can be freely modified
 * @param {Function} patchListener - optional function that will be called with all the patches produced here
 * @returns {any} a new state, or the initial state if nothing was modified
 */
export const produce: IProduce = /* @__PURE__ */ immer.produce

/**
 * Like `produce`, but `produceWithPatches` always returns a tuple
 * [nextState, patches, inversePatches] (instead of just the next state)
 */
export const produceWithPatches: IProduceWithPatches =
	/* @__PURE__ */ immer.produceWithPatches.bind(immer)

/**
 * Pass true to automatically freeze all copies created by Immer.
 *
 * Always freeze by default, even in production mode
 */
export const setAutoFreeze = /* @__PURE__ */ immer.setAutoFreeze.bind(immer)

/**
 * Pass true to enable strict shallow copy.
 *
 * By default, immer does not copy the object descriptors such as getter, setter and non-enumrable properties.
 */
export const setUseStrictShallowCopy =
	/* @__PURE__ */ immer.setUseStrictShallowCopy.bind(immer)

/**
 * Pass false to use loose iteration that only processes enumerable string properties.
 * This skips symbols and non-enumerable properties for maximum performance.
 *
 * By default, strict iteration is enabled (includes all own properties).
 */
export const setUseStrictIteration =
	/* @__PURE__ */ immer.setUseStrictIteration.bind(immer)

/**
 * Apply an array of Immer patches to the first argument.
 *
 * This function is a producer, which means copy-on-write is in effect.
 */
export const applyPatches = /* @__PURE__ */ immer.applyPatches.bind(immer)

/**
 * Create an Immer draft from the given base state, which may be a draft itself.
 * The draft can be modified until you finalize it with the `finishDraft` function.
 */
export const createDraft = /* @__PURE__ */ immer.createDraft.bind(immer)

/**
 * Finalize an Immer draft from a `createDraft` call, returning the base state
 * (if no changes were made) or a modified copy. The draft must *not* be
 * mutated afterwards.
 *
 * Pass a function as the 2nd argument to generate Immer patches based on the
 * changes that were made.
 */
export const finishDraft = /* @__PURE__ */ immer.finishDraft.bind(immer)

 * This function is actually a no-op, but can be used to cast an immutable type
 * to an draft type and make TypeScript happy
 *

 * to an immutable type and make TypeScript happy
 * @param value
 */

import {
	IProduce,
	IProduceWithPatches,
	Immer,
	Draft,
	Immutable
} from "./internal"

export {
	Draft,
	WritableDraft,
	Immutable,
	Patch,
	PatchListener,
	Producer,
	original,
	current,
	isDraft,
	isDraftable,
	NOTHING as nothing,
	DRAFTABLE as immerable,
	freeze,
	Objectish,
	StrictMode
} from "./internal"

const immer = new Immer()

/**
 * The `produce` function takes a value and a "recipe function" (whose
 * return value often depends on the base state). The recipe function is
 * free to mutate its first argument however it wants. All mutations are
 * only ever applied to a __copy__ of the base state.
 *
 * Pass only a function to create a "curried producer" which relieves you
 * from passing the recipe function every time.
 *
 * Only plain objects and arrays are made mutable. All other objects are
 * considered uncopyable.
 *
 * Note: This function is __bound__ to its `Immer` instance.
 *
 * @param {any} base - the initial state
 * @param {Function} producer - function that receives a proxy of the base state as first argument and which can be freely modified
 * @param {Function} patchListener - optional function that will be called with all the patches produced here
 * @returns {any} a new state, or the initial state if nothing was modified
 */
export const produce: IProduce = /* @__PURE__ */ immer.produce

/**
 * Like `produce`, but `produceWithPatches` always returns a tuple
 * [nextState, patches, inversePatches] (instead of just the next state)
 */
export const produceWithPatches: IProduceWithPatches =
	/* @__PURE__ */ immer.produceWithPatches.bind(immer)

/**
 * Pass true to automatically freeze all copies created by Immer.
 *
 * Always freeze by default, even in production mode
 */
export const setAutoFreeze = /* @__PURE__ */ immer.setAutoFreeze.bind(immer)

/**
 * Pass true to enable strict shallow copy.
 *
 * By default, immer does not copy the object descriptors such as getter, setter and non-enumrable properties.
 */
export const setUseStrictShallowCopy =
	/* @__PURE__ */ immer.setUseStrictShallowCopy.bind(immer)

/**
 * Pass false to use loose iteration that only processes enumerable string properties.
 * This skips symbols and non-enumerable properties for maximum performance.
 *
 * By default, strict iteration is enabled (includes all own properties).
 */
export const setUseStrictIteration =
	/* @__PURE__ */ immer.setUseStrictIteration.bind(immer)

/**
 * Apply an array of Immer patches to the first argument.
 *
 * This function is a producer, which means copy-on-write is in effect.
 */
export const applyPatches = /* @__PURE__ */ immer.applyPatches.bind(immer)

/**
 * Create an Immer draft from the given base state, which may be a draft itself.
 * The draft can be modified until you finalize it with the `finishDraft` function.
 */
export const createDraft = /* @__PURE__ */ immer.createDraft.bind(immer)

/**
 * Finalize an Immer draft from a `createDraft` call, returning the base state
 * (if no changes were made) or a modified copy. The draft must *not* be
 * mutated afterwards.
 *
 * Pass a function as the 2nd argument to generate Immer patches based on the
 * changes that were made.
 */
export const finishDraft = /* @__PURE__ */ immer.finishDraft.bind(immer)

/**
 * This function is actually a no-op, but can be used to cast an immutable type
 * to an draft type and make TypeScript happy
 *
 * @param value
 */
export let castDraft = <T>(value: T): Draft<T> => value as any

/**
 * This function is actually a no-op, but can be used to cast a mutable type
 * to an immutable type and make TypeScript happy
 * @param value
 */
export let castImmutable = <T>(value: T): Immutable<T> => value as any

```
[{"op":"replace","path":[0,"value"],"value":999},{"op":"replace","path":[0],"value":{"value":999}},{"op":"replace","path":[2],"value":{"value":1}}]
```

There are two patches for index 0:
1. `{op:"replace", path:[0,"value"], value:999}` - from the child object's value change
2. `{op:"replace", path:[0], value:{value:999}}` - from the array index reassignment

This seems like an issue with how patches are generated. The first patch is correct (updating the nested property), but the second one is redundant (replacing the entire object at index 0).

Let me think about this more carefully:

1. When we call `reverse()`, the `allIndicesReassigned_` flag is set
2. When we later access `draft[0]`, my fix creates a new draft proxy for the element that's now at index 0
3. When we mutate `draft[0].value = 999`, it modifies the draft proxy's state
4. During finalization, both the child state and the parent array state generate patches

The issue is that the parent array is generating patches for index 0 even though the child state is also generating patches for its changes. We need to make sure we don't generate redundant patches.

Looking at the `generateArrayPatches` function, there's already a check to skip indices where the child state is modified:
```javascript
const childState = copiedItem?.[DRAFT_STATE]
if (childState && childState.modified_) {
    // Skip - let the child generate its own patches
    continue
}
```

But this check happens after comparing `copiedItem !== baseItem`. 

After the reorder and mutation, `copy[0]` is the draft proxy for the element from `base[2]` with its value changed to 999, while `base[0]` is the original element with value 1. Since these are different objects, the condition `copiedItem !== baseItem` evaluates to true, so we should skip the patch generation for this index.

The child draft is marked as modified with `state.modified_ = true`, which means `childState.modified_` is true and the skip condition should trigger. However, the actual patch output shows both a nested patch for the value change and a full replacement patch for the array element itself, suggesting both levels are generating patches when only the nested one should.

The real issue is that `allIndicesReassigned_` gets set to true after the reverse operation, which causes the parent to emit a replace patch for every index. This overwrites the child's more specific patches. The solution is to have `generateArrayPatches` skip indices that have draft proxies when `allIndicesReassigned_` is true, letting the child drafts generate their own granular patches instead. All indices are then marked as reassigned. When mutations occur afterward, the code checks if a draftable value exists at that index and hasn't been drafted yet, creating a proxy if needed. The issue is that the patch generation logic treats all indices as reassigned due to the reverse operation, even those that weren't actually modified. The fix requires distinguishing between indices that were reordered versus those that were mutated—the former shouldn't generate replacement patches since the underlying objects remain unchanged, only their positions shifted. patches should be generated when the value at an index hasn't actually changed from what's in the base array. Looking at the current logic, it generates patches based solely on `allIndicesReassigned_` without checking if the value itself differs. 	StrictMode
} from "./internal"

const immer = new Immer()

/**
 * The `produce` function takes a value and a "recipe function" (whose
 * return value often depends on the base state). The recipe function is
 * free to mutate its first argument however it wants. All mutations are
 * only ever applied to a __copy__ of the base state.
 *
 * Pass only a function to create a "curried producer" which relieves you
 * from passing the recipe function every time.
 *
 * Only plain objects and arrays are made mutable. All other objects are
 * considered uncopyable.
 *
 * Note: This function is __bound__ to its `Immer` instance.
 *
 * @param {any} base - the initial state
 * @param {Function} producer - function that receives a proxy of the base state as first argument and which can be freely modified
 * @param {Function} patchListener - optional function that will be called with all the patches produced here
 * @returns {any} a new state, or the initial state if nothing was modified
 */
export const produce: IProduce = /* @__PURE__ */ immer.produce

/**
 * Like `produce`, but `produceWithPatches` always returns a tuple
 * [nextState, patches, inversePatches] (instead of just the next state)

	/* @__PURE__ */ immer.produceWithPatches.bind(immer)

 *
 * By default, immer does not copy the object descriptors such as getter, setter and non-enumrable properties.
 */

	/* @__PURE__ */ immer.setUseStrictShallowCopy.bind(immer)

## Summary

### Root Cause
The bug was in the proxy's `get` trap in `src/core/proxy.ts`. When array methods like `reverse()` or `sort()` were called on a draft array, the `handleReorderingOperation` function would:
1. Create a copy of the array via `prepareCopy(state)`
2. Execute the reordering method on the copy
3. Mark all indices as reassigned (`allIndicesReassigned_ = true`)

However, during the reordering operation, the proxy's `get` trap had an optimization that returned raw values instead of creating draft proxies for array elements. After the operation completed, when users tried to access `draft[i]` to mutate elements, the proxy's `get` trap didn't create draft proxies for these reordered values.

The check `value === peek(state.base_, prop)` failed because the value at position `i` in the copy was now a different object than the original at position `i` in the base. The code just returned this raw value without creating a draft proxy, which meant mutations to `draft[i]` were modifying the original base element directly.

### Fix
Added a new check in the proxy's `get` trap that creates draft proxies for reordered values when `allIndicesReassigned_` is true. This ensures that after a reordering operation, accessing `draft[i]` returns a proper draft proxy that tracks mutations without affecting the base state.

The fix is in `src/core/proxy.ts`:
1. Added `isDraft` to the imports
2. Added a new check after the existing `value === peek(state.base_, prop)` check:
   - When `allIndicesReassigned_` is true (set by reordering operations)
   - The value is draftable but not already a draft
   - Create a new proxy for the value and store it in the copy

This ensures that after `reverse()` or `sort()`, accessing elements returns proper draft proxies, and mutations to these elements are properly tracked without affecting the base state.
